headline: High-risk shared filesystem and git state create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and conflict hazards; Replit-side secrets raise compliance concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP; Replit Agent also reads/writes Repl workspace files. That shared filesystem bridge lets attacker-controlled content from either agent be treated as instructions by the other in default coding workflows. No stronger isolation is documented, so the interaction is plausible and not blocked.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace path
IF either agent parses file contents as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP on Gemini CLI for shared tasks
Use a handoff file format with strict schema validation
Review any file-based instructions before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment; Agent B touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Because both can read/write filesystem content and B persists Repl workspace files across sessions, sensitive material can flow between them through shared files even without explicit API sharing. The blast radius includes secrets and code.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment config are stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent copies file contents into the other agent's context or outputs
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared files
Use separate repos or directories per agent
Redact sensitive files before handoff
Rotate any secrets exposed in shared workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce file-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and modify git state, and Gemini CLI explicitly shares state via filesystem and git. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and commits can overwrite each other or corrupt history without locking. This is a default-dangerous conflict pathway with potentially irreversible repository damage.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or working tree
IF edits or commits occur without an external lock or merge gate
mitigations: Assign one agent as git writer at a time
Use separate branches per agent
Run a pre-commit diff review
Pause one agent during the other's commit window
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around git writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both agents can act on files and shell commands, so one agent's output can become the other's input in a coding workflow. Gemini CLI's MCP/tooling and Replit Agent's planner can amplify mistaken assumptions if outputs are treated as authoritative without verification. The pathway exists in default collaboration patterns, though user checkpoints reduce but do not eliminate it.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes Agent A's generated code, commands, or summaries without independent verification
IF either agent is allowed to execute downstream actions based on the other's output
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask the second agent to re-derive critical facts
Limit handoffs to structured summaries
Block direct execution of generated shell commands
requires-engineering: add automated verification of handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration in Replit-managed cloud workspaces, while Agent A handles shell environment and local files. If regulated data or production secrets are placed in the Replit workspace, residency and retention obligations may differ from local Gemini CLI handling. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data or production secrets are stored in the Replit workspace
IF the deployment or retention policy for that data differs between the two environments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Store secrets only in approved secret managers
Confirm residency and retention settings before use
Use synthetic data for cross-agent work
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy
